items.summary: An open-source (MIT) multi-agent orchestration framework: Antigravity architects and audits, Claude Code writes the code, Codex tests and ships, with each phase handing off through a standardized HANDOFF.md. It ships relay, debate and audit workflows plus a tri-agent CLI (doctor, handoff, run), write-scope checks and an audit trail; created November 10 and built on the Python standard library alone, with no extra dependencies.
items.title: Tri-Agent Orchestrator: Relay Antigravity, Claude Code and Codex through one handoff contract (open-sourced Nov 10, MIT)

items.summary: A free desktop app that turns one sentence into a finished website, slide deck, video, logo or research report: it shows an editable plan first and asks before any risky step. It reuses the agents you already pay for — Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Antigravity CLI and a dozen more — at no extra cost, and across your machines it offers remote desktop, one shared clipboard and agents that keep running on another computer, plus a web version for remote use. Launched on Product Hunt on November 14.
items.title: Tesseract: A free desktop agent that turns one sentence into finished work, with agents that keep going on another computer (Product Hunt, Nov 14)

items.summary: A proxy-style tool: point your LLM calls at gate.three.dev and it scores your live traffic, groups failures into modes ranked by severity and flags newly appeared ones as New — no SDK to install. It then hands each failing request and its cause to your coding agent over MCP to write the fix. Supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Azure OpenAI and LiteLLM; generally available November 10 and on Product Hunt November 12.
items.title: three.dev: Finds your live agent's silent failures, ranks them by severity and hands the fix to your coding agent (generally available Nov 10)
